canonical_name: Babai deterministic quasipolynomial-time Graph Isomorphism algorithm family
literal_source_claim_zh: 图同构的准多项式算法
literal_source_claim_en: A quasipolynomial algorithm for graph isomorphism.
source_attribution: Laszlo Babai, 2015 (catalog metadata; post-fix source family inspected independently)
provisional_human_claim_not_frozen: A deterministic algorithm decides whether two finite graphs are isomorphic with worst-case running time exp((log n)^(O(1))) in the number n of vertices.
statement_blocker: The source-level theorem is identifiable, but the repository and source shorthand do not fix a binder-complete formal proposition. They omit a canonical graph-pair serialization, malformed-input policy, Boolean versus witness or coset output, exact deterministic machine and primitive-cost model, vertex-count versus encoding-length bridge, constants and threshold in exp(C*(log n)^c), rounding and small-input conventions, and the checked Graph Isomorphism to String Isomorphism reduction. The v2 proof also requires reconciliation with the UPCC and Design Lemma corrections and the post-fix reconstruction. Choosing these details at intake would invent proposition-changing formal scope.
target_decision: preserve the stable human Graph Isomorphism quasipolynomial-time result while requiring independent approval of a complete corrected source bundle and an exact formal computation/bound contract before statement elaboration
domain_and_universes: Open at formal level: an approved statement must fix finite graph and vertex representations, simple versus colored/directed/multigraph scope, graph-pair serialization, input alphabet, malformed inputs, Boolean/witness/coset output, deterministic machine state and alphabets, step cost, time codomain, size measure, and every finiteness, decidability, and universe context.
conclusion: Provisional human conclusion only: a deterministic Graph Isomorphism solver is correct and has worst-case quasipolynomial running time. Exact formal output, totality, constants, threshold, size variable, and bound representation remain open.
degenerate_case_status: No case is excluded at intake; statement work must resolve empty and singleton graphs, unequal orders, isolated vertices, graph variants, invalid encodings, zero/one logarithms, natural rounding, asymptotic thresholds, and every small-input output convention.
candidate_scope_not_credited: correctness and totality of a fully specified deterministic Graph Isomorphism decision procedure
worst-case quasipolynomial runtime of that exact procedure
a conjunction of decision correctness, totality, and the runtime bound

Coset Intersection or colored-graph refinements as separately owned branches
degenerate_cases_to_resolve: empty, singleton, unequal-order, edgeless, complete, and isolated-vertex graphs
simple undirected versus directed, colored, labeled, looped, or parallel-edge graph models
same versus different vertex carriers and Boolean versus witness or coset output

vertex count versus encoded length and polynomial overhead of graph-to-string conversion
deterministic totality, halting, primitive-step cost, uniformity, and worst-case quantification
logarithm base, constants, exponents, ceilings, thresholds, and natural-number time bounds
excluded_substitutions: plain graph-isomorphism decidability, brute-force enumeration, or membership in NP
